business_rules: Shipment origin and destination must be different (RF-03).
Shipment origin remains fixed throughout the lifecycle (RF-04).
Registration may complete before a route is defined; such shipments are 'unrouted' (RF-05, RF-11).
Delivery deadline is mandatory and used as a planning criterion (RF-06).
Origin/destination must be chosen from previously registered locations (RF-07).
A candidate route is valid only if it satisfies origin, final destination, and deadline (RF-09).
A changed destination must be neither the origin nor the current destination (RF-15).
A changed destination triggers route reassessment and possible re-routing (RF-16, RF-17).
Every logistics event must reference an existing shipment, location, and (for loading/unloading) trip (RF-32, RF-33, RF-34, RF-36).
Events other than loading/unloading do not require a trip identifier (RF-35).
Recording a valid event updates status and recalculates transport status, location, next step, and plan adherence (RF-37, RF-38).
Execution differing from the planned route marks the shipment off route (RF-39, RNF-64).
Unloading at final destination marks arrival; recipient pickup marks logistics completion (RF-40, RF-41).
No invalid event may alter shipment state (RNF-47).
Origin/destination/deadline/route rules apply uniformly across all channels (RNF-48).
Status is recalculated on any relevant planning or execution change (RNF-49).
The tracking model is unique regardless of channel (RNF-67).

microservices.responsibility: Register new shipments with origin, destination, and delivery deadline from controlled location lists, assign unique tracking identifiers, associate selected routes, and support destination change/replanning triggers. Provides the booking web/REST interface and consolidated administrative views grouped by business status (unrouted, in transit, collected).

Compute and query candidate routes compatible with a shipment's origin, final destination, and delivery deadline; present route legs (loading/unloading points, trips, planned dates); and reassess routes when destination changes or shipments deviate. Wraps the pathfinder graph-traversal subsystem.

Look up a shipment by tracking identifier to present current status, last known location, ETA, event history (distinguishing expected from off-plan events), and geographic support. microservices.responsibility: Register new shipments with origin, destination, and delivery deadline from controlled location lists, assign unique tracking identifiers, associate selected routes, and support destination change/replanning triggers. Provides the booking web/REST interface and consolidated administrative views grouped by business status (unrouted, in transit, collected).

Compute and query candidate routes compatible with a shipment's origin, final destination, and delivery deadline; present route legs (loading/unloading points, trips, planned dates); and reassess routes when destination changes or shipments deviate. Wraps the pathfinder graph-traversal subsystem.

Record receipt, loading, unloading, customs, and pickup events tied to an existing shipment, location, and (for loading/unloading) trip; validate and reject invalid events; recalculate transport status, known location, next step, and plan adherence; and mark arrival, completion, and off-route conditions. Accepts events via operational REST, mobile, and periodic file processing channels using a unified event model.

Look up a shipment by tracking identifier to present current status, last known location, ETA, event history (distinguishing expected from off-plan events), and geographic support. Maintains traceability sufficient to reconstruct the shipment lifecycle including occurrence/recording times and rejected attempts, keeping a unique tracking model across all channels.

microservices.responsibility: Register new shipments with origin, destination, and delivery deadline from controlled location lists, assign unique tracking identifiers, associate selected routes, and handle destination change/replanning triggers by requesting route reassessment. Provides the booking web/REST interface and consolidated administrative views grouped by business status (unrouted, in transit, collected). Consumes recalculated status from the Logistics Event Service rather than recomputing operational status itself.

Compute and query candidate routes compatible with a shipment's origin, final destination, and delivery deadline; present route legs (loading/unloading points, trips, planned dates); and reassess/replan routes when destination changes or shipments deviate. Wraps the pathfinder graph-traversal subsystem. Invoked by Booking (initial routing and destination-change replanning) and by the Logistics Event Service when off-route detection requires reassessment.

Record receipt, loading, unloading, customs, and pickup events tied to an existing shipment, location, and (for loading/unloading) trip; validate and reject invalid events; and act as the authoritative owner of status recalculation, computing transport status, known location, next step, and plan adherence, and marking arrival, completion, and off-route conditions. On off-route or deviation detection, requests route reassessment from the Routing Service. Accepts events via operational REST, mobile, and periodic file processing channels using a unified event model. Booking and Tracking consume its recalculated status as read-side consumers.

Look up a shipment by tracking identifier to present current status, last known location, ETA, event history (distinguishing expected from off-plan events), and geographic support, reading recalculated status from the Logistics Event Service rather than recomputing it. Maintains traceability sufficient to reconstruct the shipment lifecycle including occurrence/recording times and rejected attempts, keeping a unique tracking model across all channels.
